confidence: medium (code read; live POST probe was denied by the harness)
exploitability: Any scripted client; sends matching Origin and Host headers, no auth needed
problem: NEXT_PUBLIC_ORACLE_ENABLED=false only hides the UI. The paid /api/oracle and /api/quiz routes check only ORACLE_KILL_SWITCH and a same-origin check that a non-browser client can forge by setting Origin equal to Host.
impact: The Oracle is not actually off in production; anyone can still spend Anthropic/Groq tokens up to 10/hr/IP and the 500/day global cap. Operator intent and real state differ.
fix: Make the server routes return 503 unless the same enabled flag (or ORACLE_KILL_SWITCH) says on; keep the kill switch set in prod. Do not treat Origin as auth.
verification: Set the flag off, POST with matching Origin, expect 503 before any grounding or model call.

problem: Oracle, quiz, search and analytics limiters fail open: a timeout returns success and a thrown error propagates. Only newsletter buckets use failClosed.
impact: During an Upstash incident per-IP limits stop applying to billed search embeddings. Oracle/quiz still hit the global incr counter, which throws, so spend stays bounded.
fix: Use failClosed for oracle, quiz and search buckets (they cost money per admission).
verification: Unit test with a mocked limiter returning reason:'timeout'; expect allowed:false.

problem: The PostHog reverse proxy has no rate limit, no request body size cap and no origin check, and runs as a force-dynamic nodejs function streaming request bodies upstream. The path allowlist itself holds (checked: /ingest/static/../api/projects/ returns 404).
impact: Invocation cost and PostHog quota can be burned by a script, and spoofed events pollute analytics.
fix: Cap content-length, add an IP bucket via the existing Upstash limiter, and require a same-origin Origin header.
verification: curl with a 5 MB body to /ingest/e/ and expect 413.

problem: The CSP report endpoint is a no-op 204 stub; violations (and the degraded unsafe-inline mode) are never observed. It is also unauthenticated and unbounded.
impact: No signal if a hash drifts or an injection is blocked; CSP regressions are only caught by e2e.
fix: Forward to Sentry with a size cap and rate limit, or drop report-to.
verification: POST a sample report-to payload and confirm it appears in Sentry.

exploitability: Needs the manifest to be unreadable at runtime
problem: If csp-manifest.json cannot be read or fetched, proxy serves script-src with 'unsafe-inline' (fail-open) and only logs once. The fetch target is request.nextUrl.origin.
impact: A deployment fault silently removes script injection protection site-wide. Production currently serves the strict policy (header captured 2026-11-04).
fix: Alert on x-csp-mode: degraded in monitoring, or fail the build when the public manifest is absent.
verification: Capture response headers after deploy and assert no x-csp-mode header.

problem: pull_request_target job checks out a PR branch with persist-credentials and a PAT (AUTOMATION_TOKEN) then runs pnpm install. Gated on dependabot actor, same-repo head, --ignore-scripts and --ignore-pnpmfile, so risk is low.
impact: A compromised dependabot branch could reach a write token during install (pnpm config from the branch is still read).
fix: Use persist-credentials:false for the install and pass the token only to the push step.
verification: Review workflow after change; confirm lockfile-only job has no token in git config.
resolution: #284: checkout persist-credentials false; token only in push step env. Unexercised until next Dependabot PR

problem: 2 moderate advisories reported, glob >=9 <=14.0.1 reached through the Sentry bundler plugin.
impact: Affects build machines, not runtime serverless code; no hostile glob input.
fix: Add a pnpm override to glob >=14.0.2 once compatible, or wait for Sentry to bump.
resolution: PR #290 merged 2bd76313: webhook answers 413 above 64 KB via shared readCappedStream; two tests fail on main, pass on branch; CI green incl. E2E + visual.

problem: The event sink accepts a client-chosen distinctId and arbitrary properties for allowlisted event names.
impact: Analytics data can be spoofed under another visitor id; no PII or auth impact.
fix: Ignore client distinctId and derive a server-side anonymous id, or document as untrusted.
verification: Send two events with the same distinctId from different IPs; they merge.
resolution: Client distinctId is intentional (joins survey to PostHog person, QuizRetentionSurvey.tsx:57). Public PostHog key already allows any distinct_id direct to PostHog, so the sink adds no capability; event names allowlisted and properties schema-validated

exploitability: low: platform body limit applies, signature check rejects forged payloads after the read
problem: The Resend webhook reads the whole request body with req.text() and no byte cap, before the signature check. Every other body-reading route uses readJsonBody with a cap.
impact: An unauthenticated caller can make the function buffer bodies up to the platform limit, costing memory and invocation time.
fix: Read through the shared capped reader and answer 413 above a small cap before verifying the signature.
verification: Unit test: oversized chunked body returns 413 and verify is never called.
resolution: PR #290 merged 2bd76313: webhook answers 413 above 64 KB via shared readCappedStream; two tests fail on main, pass on branch; CI green incl. E2E + visual.
